entries.heading: THE HOUSE
entries.telling: You keep a house of heroes for 25 years, a turn a year: a summer of quests, a winter at the hearth, then the turn of the year. After the last summer the Sealed Door opens. Everything before it is raising a family that can walk through it.
entries.telling_template: You keep a house of heroes for % years, a turn a year: a summer of quests, a winter at the hearth, then the turn of the year. After the last summer the Sealed Door opens. Everything before it is raising a family that can walk through it.

entries.heading: SUMMER
entries.telling: Four quests are posted. Drag heroes onto their seats. A quest tests one aptitude: what the party brings, plus two dice less 7, against what it needs. Beat it by 4 for a triumph; miss it by more than 4 for a disaster. Anyone left at home heals a wound.

entries.heading: RENOWN
entries.telling: The house lives on its renown. Quests won earn it, and so does a tale told at the long table. A disaster costs it, and so does every quest left unanswered: more the higher the house stands, since more is expected of it. At 0 the house closes.

entries.heading: TROUBLE
entries.telling: A place left unanswered grows troubled, up to 2. A troubled quest has room for fewer, asks more of each who goes, is more dangerous, and pays more. Answer it and it eases, however it goes. Every quest asks a little more as the years pass.

entries.heading: DREAMS AND LEGACIES
entries.telling: Every hero wants one thing, in three steps. A quest that would move a dream on names the dreamer. A dream fulfilled settles the hero and leaves a legacy: an heirloom of +2, a tale that earns renown every year, or a blessing on the dreamer's line.

entries.heading: FEARS
entries.telling: Against what they fear a hero brings less, and comes home with dread. At 5 dread they break, and refuse it for ever. With someone bonded beside them, a success gives courage instead; 3 courage conquers the fear, and it becomes a strength. The fire sheds dread.

entries.heading: DESTINIES
entries.telling: The Seer speaks over each hero when they come of age or arrive. Under each prophecy is its doom and its gift, exactly as the game applies them. Read them before you send anyone anywhere: a crown, a fire and a bed are all kept.

entries.heading: BONDS
entries.telling: Made on the road and by the fire. Two successes together make friends, a disaster makes rivals. Spouses, parents and children are strongest. Bonded heroes bring more together, steady each other against fear, and grieve each other's deaths.

entries.heading: WINTER
entries.telling: Ten seats, and more hands than seats. By the fire: heal, shed dread. The training yard: learn alone, or under one who knows more. The garden: court. The long table: tell the tale. The benches: teach a child. Whoever is left in the hall gains nothing.

entries.heading: TEACHING
entries.telling: Alone, a hero trains their calling, up to 6. A teacher passes on their best aptitude, up to their own; veterans and elders teach well and the young learn fast. A youth learns from any quest that succeeds, and the least able learns from a triumph.

entries.heading: COURTING AND CHILDREN
entries.telling: Two may wed when both are 18 or older, no more than 15 years apart, and not kin. From the year after, they may have a child each winter while both are 18 to 45, up to 3. The house holds 12 in all, 6 of them children.

entries.heading: GROWING UP
entries.telling: From 6 a child is taught on a bench, up to 4 in each aptitude; their first teacher decides their calling. At 12 they come of age, hear the Seer and may quest, 1 short in every aptitude until 20. From 40 Might fades and Wits grows; from 55 more so, and each winter may be the last.

entries.heading: HERITAGE
entries.telling: A child takes a share of both parents' aptitudes, may take a parent's fear, likelier if that parent broke, or be born brave where a parent conquered it, and inherits every blessing on the line. A child whose parent fell on a quest dreams of avenging them.

entries.heading: DEATH, HEIRS AND GHOSTS
entries.telling: A second wound kills. When someone dies with an heirloom or a dream undone, you choose the heir, kin first. The heir takes the heirloom and carries the dream on. Left to no one, the dream walks as a ghost, and a quest to lay it returns until it is won.

entries.heading: THE SEALED DOOR
entries.telling: Three locks, of Might, Wits and Spirit, tried in turn by the same four. Each lock weighs all the four bring: aptitude, heirlooms, blessings, conquered fears, every bond between them, and the Seer's promise. Fear of the dark or the cold counts against them.

entries.heading: READING
entries.telling: Point at a hero for their sheet, at a quest for its odds in full, at headings for how they work. On a card, red is wounded, grey is old, purple pips are dread, a gold pip is settled. The family shows everyone who ever lived here, and what was said of them.
